title: Developer experience: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site ops, and top support issues (Playbook)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's developer experience (DevEx) documentation standards and operating procedures for SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site publishing, and the canonical list of top support issues with fixes. It is intended for DevEx authors, SDK maintainers, solutions engineers, and on-call support engineers responsible for developer-facing documentation.

1) Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Ensure consistent, discoverable, and up-to-date developer documentation that reduces time-to-value for customers and minimizes support load.
- Scope: SDK guides (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go), quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures (publishing, CI), and canonical fixes for top support issues. Does not cover internal-only runbooks unrelated to developer onboarding.

2) Ownership and roles
- Content owner: DevEx Documentation Team (engineers + technical writers).
- Reviewers: SDK owners for each language (see related_pages).
- Release authority: DevEx lead or assigned doc owner for a given package.
- Escalation path: doc author -> DevEx lead -> SDK owner -> Engineering manager.

3) Document types and canonical structure
All docs must follow the standard structure for readability and automation:
- Title (short, descriptive)
- Short summary (1-2 sentences)
- Audience (who should read this)
- Prerequisites (accounts, API keys, versions)
- Quickstart / Example (copy-paste runnable)
- Explanations (API semantics, config options, caveats)
- Troubleshooting (top 3 issues for this page)
- Related pages and links
- Change log / last updated line

4) SDK guide standards (per-language)
- Supported languages: Python, TypeScript/Node, Go. Additional community SDKs allowed but must pass review.
- Versioning: Include SDK version in the header and compatibility table with API versions.
- Code examples: Must be minimal, idiomatic, and executable. Prefer snippets that can be copy-pasted into a REPL or file.
- Authentication: Show both API-key and environment-variable patterns.
- Error handling: Include typical error classes and a brief retry/backoff pattern.
- Tests: Each SDK guide must have a small runnable sample test or smoke-check (CI step).

Example (Python snippet to include in SDK guides):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
response = client.generate("Translate to French: Hello world")
print(response.text)
```

5) Quickstarts and templates
- Purpose: Provide minimal artifacts that get a developer from 0 to a working integration in <10 minutes.
- Quickstart types: CLI tutorial, web app example, bot example, serverless example.
- Templates: GitHub starter repos with README, LICENSE, dependencies, and a single integration file. Templates must include a prefilled .gitignore and a README section labeled "How to run locally".
- Directory structure for a quickstart repo:
  - README.md
  - .env.example
  - src/ (single example file per language)
  - tests/smoke_test.py or test_main.go
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml (simple publish/test workflow)

6) API examples and idioms
- Keep examples focused: one feature / one snippet. Avoid multi-feature monoliths.
- Response streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured output examples must be included in the API examples library.
- Provide both synchronous and streaming variants where applicable.
- Include JSON schema examples for structured output and a small example of how to validate it.

API example (Node streaming pattern):
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-alpha-chat' })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```

7) Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow)
- Authoring: Use Markdown in the docs repo. Each page maps to a Confluence-page-like entry and must pass linting.
- Branch workflow: feature branch -> doc review PR -> QA check -> merge to main -> automatic site deploy.
- Required checks on PRs: spelling check, link check, code snippet execution (where feasible), and accessibility lint.
- Release cadence: Docs are deployed on merge to main. Major changes should be coordinated with SDK releases and announced in #devex and release notes.
- Emergency fix flow: If a production doc contains incorrect security or breaking API info, create a hotfix branch, mark PR with label "hotfix/docs", and notify #devex and #oncall.

CI example (GitHub Actions steps to include in .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml):
- name: Lint docs
  run: npm run docs:lint
- name: Run snippet smoke tests
  run: pytest docs/snippets/tests || true
- name: Deploy
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
  run: ./scripts/deploy-site.sh

8) Review checklist (must be satisfied before merging)
1. Accurate and concise summary present.
2. Code samples run without modification (CI smoke tests pass).
3. SLO-sensitive content (latency/cost) includes data source and date.
4. Security considerations called out (PII, encryption).
5. Links use stable internal URLs or external references.
6. Reviewer sign-off from relevant SDK owner.

9) Top support issues and canonical fixes (developer-facing)
- Issue: Authentication failures (401 / invalid key)
  - Symptom: Requests return 401 with message "invalid API key".
  - Root cause: Developer used a project-scoped key that was rotated or pasted an expired token; or environment variable not set in the runtime.
  - Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY exported and not wrapped in quotes. Show command: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-..." (in docs include OS-specific instructions). If key rotated, instruct to regenerate in Console and update secrets manager.
  - Related docs: auth guide, secrets management template.

- Issue: Streaming responses hang or time out
  - Symptom: Partial output then connection closed / hung.
  - Root cause: Client-side HTTP library not reading streaming chunks, or reverse proxy (e.g., older NGINX) buffering responses.
  - Canonical fix: Provide streaming-capable example (Node fetch/axios with response.body.getReader()). Add note to disable buffering in proxies: proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on.

- Issue: High token usage / unexpected costs
  - Symptom: Customer reports spikes in token consumption.
  - Root cause: Model choice mismatch, missing stop sequences, or loop generating additional prompts.
  - Canonical fix: Recommend model with lower token cost for high-volume workloads, add stop tokens, apply prefix caching, and enable per-route rate limits. Include a cost-debugging checklist.

- Issue: SDK compatibility errors after release
  - Symptom: Runtime exceptions referencing removed parameters or changed return shapes.
  - Root cause: Breaking change not documented or consumer pinned to an incompatible minor version.
  - Canonical fix: Maintain compatibility table in the SDK guide, include migration notes, and provide code recipes for common migrations.

10) Canonical troubleshooting snippets (to include on relevant docs pages)
- Validate API key (curl):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/health
- Streaming healthcheck (Node example):
```js
// basic streaming check
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream', { headers })
if (!res.ok) throw new Error('stream failed: ' + res.status)
for await (const chunk of res.body) console.log(chunk.toString())
```

11) Metrics, quality, and SLAs for docs
- Pages with runnable examples must maintain a <2% CI failure rate for snippet tests (tracked weekly).
- Median time to fix a hotfix label docs issue: 8 hours.
- Docs-related support tickets should be reduced by 10% quarter-over-quarter as measured by the support tagging system.

12) Communication and change log
- Announce major doc changes in #devex with a one-paragraph summary, impact, and links.
- Maintain a CHANGELOG.md at the root of the docs repo listing notable edits and dates.

13) Templates and automation
- Provide a ready-to-use PR template for doc changes that includes the Review checklist and testing instructions.
- Automate snippet execution where feasible. Use a small matrix in CI to run language-specific smoke tests.

14) Frequently updated appendix items (maintained as separate pages)
- Code of conduct for examples (avoid PII samples).
- Model cost table and recommended defaults for common workloads.
- Internal list of SDK owners and contact points.

15) Related references
- Developer Experience Docs Playbook (canonical): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-playbook-2026
- SDK repo templates: /github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates
- DevEx CI config: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/devex-sdk-quickstarts-and-api-examples-2026
